title: Certify normalized Gaussian calls through full Toeplitz circuits
body:
I connect the retained normalized Gaussian `Tsec` function and its adjacent
`full_plan` call to requested-precision rational coefficients and the complete
logical forward/inverse circuit.

For dyadic size `N`, rational `c>0`, `|s|<=1/2`, and
`T[i,j]=exp(-pi*c*((j-i)^2-2*s*(j-i)))`, I derive one budget for truncation,
coefficient quantization and circuit rounding. I prove error below `2^-t`
against the ideal normalized matrix and its inverse, with online widths

`O(F0 + t + log N + log R + 1/c)`.

I rederive the finite-cap bound `||T_b^-1||_(1,infinity) <= N*exp(pi/(4*c))`
for all leading sections, including both half-shift endpoints. I construct
a rational upper allowance from Mason Hale's retained interval routines,
quantize each offset once and require the same matrix at the full compiler.
I use perturbation to establish both leading-section admission and the
inverse-reference error. I use the previous full-circuit result for the
polynomial intermediate-amplification bound and global gate allocation.

I preserve the source's `j-i` orientation, symbolic cancellation at the
diagonal and exact diagonal ones. I retain both source statements and both
adjacent callsite assignments, substituting exact arithmetic and the
certified exponential table. I reject an explicit cutoff whose tail exceeds
its allowance. I preserve the previous four complete scientific receipts.

Evidence:

- Nine Gaussian cases, 4,527 gates and 38 rounded forward/inverse states.
  I include both half shifts, a near-half shift, an interior negative shift,
  nonzero paid truncation, a 512-bit incoming vector and two requested precisions.
- I compare exact leading-section inverses and finer scalar interval
  references, paying the finer reference's residual error. I use the same
  declared interval backend for those references.
- Sixteen controls cover source orientation, normalization, altered roots,
  missing pi, insufficient coefficient precision, unpaid truncation and
  discarded incoming grids.
- Gaussian scientific receipt:
  `0a0548963b8132b430f43b8534abbd4220b93a138eb9e0a28a9cfd7432922928`.

I run the old full verifier and the Gaussian verifier sequentially in the
existing two 300-second slots. I retain eight normal/optimized commands
and a total timeout budget of 1,200 seconds.

At head `66b95cc916552f487203be14fd99a7aea0bdd78e`, I passed the
43-file committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export
integrity check. All eight registered and Git-free commands pass;
all 44 exported files stayed unchanged. The combined full/Gaussian
commands took 31.914 and 32.200 seconds in the export.
Archive SHA256: `b81a13321adc9b33edc61beb4e3ec46de4c860a19e97ab1d14b49377756dcad6`;
receipt SHA256: `fcd5c528c84c1a7703d6c9bc2290994f77a5916806309309e5a6b6b06231f059`.
I matched all ten successful [hosted records](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39470174495)
to the export, including all five scientific digests and the unchanged-input
step. Test merge `4b24dc0e4012f2816dedff2c29e5fef5f40edfe8` has the exact
base/head parents and publication tree `4b2d0e5a71b527bee3459e623293acefea5740e5`.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/rational-unitary-fft
```

I start from canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`,
priority revision 7. I preserve full revision
`7ab1bc8973cc9e606053c65f094ca3abc4a42fee` and its
[hosted evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39463338955),
along with the earlier FFT, triangle and generator revisions.
[Discussion4202](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4202)
records the expansion decision, source pins and overlap coverage.
Before publication I refreshed unchanged main, inspected 12 recent
open PR records and 5/783 hub comments, and checked the unchanged
feedback state on this PR.

Reviewers must assess the universal arguments separately from the finite
receipts. Raw Gaussian gauges, alpha scaling, common-reference assembly,
physical coefficient preparation/delivery and complete tape costs remain
open. I leave the selected frontier unchanged.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
I credit Mason Hale/PR2313 for interval arithmetic and existing dense
Gaussian/integer execution; Jeremy Kothe/IdeaOuter for the shifted source;
Vlado Vojdanovski/PR1673 for q-LDU and the recursive circuit; Chafik
Boukhalfa/PR628 for phases; Cinna Davis for the later caller; and the
classical Vandermonde, q-binomial, Fourier and Neumann-series methods.
I retain ToikY's distinct [Schur-closure result](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4209)
and James Reed's [scoped audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4205#issuecomment-6295524563)
at the earlier `fdcdc269` head. Internal agents belong to our author process.
